findings.title: Guarded file replacement overwrites concurrent in-place user edits
evidence: The replacement guard compares inode identity only. After the agent reads an open file, an editor or background job can truncate/write the SAME inode. Publication still succeeds and replaces the newer contents with output computed from the old contents. Both relative edit and guarded write(overwrite=true) use this boundary.
findings.required_change: Carry a content/version snapshot from the read into publication and reject stale content, not just pathname/inode replacement. Revalidate the exchanged-out file before deleting it and restore it on mismatch; retain existing symlink and identity protections. Cover the absolute-path edit/write publication paths too, where only the approved parent currently crosses the await boundary.
findings.verification: Reproduction patch docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-core.patch, test release_review_probe_guarded_replacement_preserves_concurrent_in_place_edit fails on 6021ba1: stale replacement returns Ok and deletes concurrent user change. Add deterministic tests for a same-inode write after read and during publication for relative/absolute edit and guarded overwrite; latest user contents must survive and caller must be told to reread. Run cargo test paths and edit/overwrite tests.

findings.title: Distilling to a user-selected file changes its existing parent directory permissions
evidence: --distill-learned-skill-out /shared/project/draft.json calls ensure_private_directory on the existing destination parent, then private_atomic_create_sync repeats it. On Unix this unconditionally chmods /shared/project to 0700, removing group/other access. It happens even if the destination already exists and export fails.
findings.required_change: Separate private application-state directory creation from user-selected export destinations. Preserve permissions/ACLs of existing output parents, keep the new draft file private and create-only, and preserve no-follow/atomic guarantees. Audit analogous explicit export-path callers without weakening app-private storage defaults.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_distill_preserves_destination_directory_mode in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-core.patch fails: expected 0755, observed 0700. Test 0755 and 0770 existing parents on successful export and AlreadyExists, default private output directory, symlink rejection and file 0600. Run cargo test --features skills distill.

findings.title: Edit tool has no input/output file size bound and can exhaust the parent
evidence: Read and write receive max_text_file_size (default 1 MiB), but EditTool does not. It reads the entire regular file into an unbounded Vec before even validating the edit mode. A tiny edit call against a multi-GB log/generated file allocates the full contents in the unsandboxed parent, followed by matching and output copies; replace_all can additionally expand output far beyond the file cap.
findings.required_change: Thread the configured text-file budget into EditTool in all agent constructors. Check metadata and perform a bounded read that also catches file growth; validate requested replacement sizes and aggregate final output size before allocating/publishing. Reject invalid edit argument modes before reading large files. Preserve valid bounded file behavior.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_edit_obeys_default_file_size_limit on 6021ba1 edits a 2 MiB file successfully despite the default 1 MiB cap. Add limit-1/limit/limit+1 tests, custom limits, growth-after-stat and replace_all expansion; rejected edits must leave bytes unchanged. Run cargo test edit plus feature-isolated tests.

findings.title: One unsafe saved-session entry prevents lookup of unrelated healthy sessions
evidence: Directory enumeration propagates read_private_string errors with ?. A single broken symlink, unsafe file, or entry disappearing during iteration aborts the whole search, even when the requested valid session was loaded. Session selection/resume can become unavailable until the user manually repairs an unrelated entry.
findings.required_change: Keep exact-ID loading fail-closed, but isolate per-entry errors in multi-session discovery: skip unsafe/unreadable/raced-away entries with a bounded diagnostic and continue collecting healthy matches. Apply the requested limit to successfully decoded sessions rather than candidates so bad recent files cannot hide older valid sessions.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_one_bad_session_does_not_hide_healthy_sessions saves one valid session and unrelated broken.json symlink; exact-prefix discovery returns Err. Add tests for prefix/name/recent/workspace queries with bad entry before/after healthy ones, invalid JSON and concurrent deletion; never follow or mutate the unsafe entry.

findings.title: A language server that stops reading stdin hangs read/edit/write tools
evidence: write_owned_frame waits for the shared stdin mutex and writes/flushes a complete frame with no deadline. The response timeout in request starts only AFTER the write. Document synchronization notifications have no response timeout at all. A server that initializes successfully then stops reading fills its pipe; syncing an ordinary 1 MiB document blocks the tool and its shared/exclusive tool lane indefinitely.
findings.required_change: Use a deadline covering writer-lock acquisition plus frame write/flush and response wait. Apply an explicit bounded notification deadline too. Treat a timed-out partial frame as a terminal transport failure using the existing TransportWriteGuard, reap the server, and let file tools report their completed mutation with bounded diagnostics.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_lsp_stalled_writer_is_bounded in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch: fixture initializes then stops reading; 1 MiB sync_text requires the external 500ms cancellation to return. That short timeout is a probe, not a proposed production limit. Add virtual-time or configurable-deadline tests for blocked writer and queued writer, require bounded return/child reaping, and verify subsequent file tools continue. Run cargo test --features lsp lsp_process.

findings.title: MCP collision renaming can create duplicate registered tool names
evidence: Only duplicate BARE names are counted. Servers alpha/probe and beta/probe rename to alpha__probe and beta__probe, while gamma's originally unique alpha__probe stays unchanged. The collected catalog now contains alpha__probe twice. This reintroduces ambiguous model schemas and downstream tool replacement, so a requested tool can route to the wrong server.
findings.required_change: Allocate final registered names against one complete used-name set, including unchanged names and every generated name; handle same-server duplicate definitions too. Use an injective escape/suffix policy and enforce provider-compatible name/length restrictions. Keep actual wire names and permission identities separate and stable.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_mcp_generated_names_cannot_collide in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch starts three real stdio fixtures and returns [alpha__probe,beta__probe,alpha__probe]. Regression should assert uniqueness plus calls reach all three intended servers with distinct permissions. Cover separator collisions (server a__b/tool c vs a/tool b__c) and repeated definitions.

findings.title: MCP structured-only tool results are silently returned as empty output
evidence: The success path iterates result.content and ignores result.structured_content entirely. A successful result with content:[] and structuredContent:{answer:42} becomes only empty MCP delimiters. The model loses the result and may repeat a side-effecting call or invent an answer.
findings.required_change: Preserve structuredContent in model-visible output with the existing size/spill limits and untrusted-content delimiters. Define deterministic behavior when both text content and structuredContent exist so data is available without unbounded duplication. Also make unsupported content kinds explicit instead of presenting an unexplained empty success.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_mcp_preserves_structured_only_result in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch calls a real fixture returning answer:42; current output is '[mcp output begins]\n> \n[mcp output ends]'. Add structured-only, mixed, large structured result and isError tests through McpTool::call; no repeated execution should be needed to obtain the value.

findings.title: Streaming a code fence repeatedly reparses the whole fence quadratically
evidence: Every newly completed code line scans and reparses from the fence start because no stable boundary is published inside a fence. A deterministic 1,000-line, 19,008-byte fenced response sends 9,517,500 bytes through the markdown parser (~501x source size). Long generated code, logs, lists and paragraphs stall the UI as the response grows; the mixed-paragraph benchmark does not cover this path.
findings.required_change: Maintain incremental fence/list rendering state or render bounded live tails with completed rows retained until finalization. Avoid cloning the full stable row prefix on every chunk as part of the performance fix. Preserve exact finalized Markdown behavior and width-change invalidation.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_long_fence_parsing_is_linear in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch measures parser work, not noisy wall time; fails at 9,517,500 parsed bytes for 19,008 source bytes. Add 1k/2k/4k-line scaling tests for fenced code and long lists/paragraphs, and measure total layout work/allocation as well as parser bytes; require near-linear work and equivalent final output.

findings.title: Streaming Markdown mistakes a shorter code fence for a closing delimiter
evidence: The boundary scanner tracks only fence character, not opening delimiter length or closing-line validity. After a four-backtick opening, an embedded triple-backtick code line is treated as a close. A following blank line caches an unsafe stable boundary, so '# literal header' is rendered as a heading while streaming even though it remains literal code; finalization visibly changes the content.
findings.required_change: Match the actual Markdown fence rules: retain opening character/length and indentation, require a valid closing line of sufficient length and no non-whitespace suffix, and keep invalid shorter delimiters inside the fence. Share parser state where possible instead of duplicating an incomplete grammar.
findings.verification: release_review_probe_long_fence_delimiter_streaming_matches_final_render in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch proves streamed rows lose the literal '#' while finalized rows retain it. Add chunk-boundary tests for 3/4/5 delimiters, tildes, trailing text, indentation and embedded blank lines; compare rendered text and style before/after finalization.

findings.title: Nightly evaluation drops the first persona metric and never runs the library axis
evidence: The current baseline's Nightly harness evaluation run 34199175478 failed although all fixture/persona tests passed. With --nocapture --test-threads=1 libtest prefixes the first persona JSON record with 'test ... ... '. grep '^PERSONA_EVAL ' extracts only eight of nine records, so -eq 9 fails. The learned-skill library-axis step and metrics upload are skipped. Current Python policy tests merely assert the broken grep/count strings are present.
findings.required_change: Emit metrics to dedicated JSONL artifacts or parse a known record prefix independent of libtest's progress text, validate JSON/schema/counts, and test the actual extractor on representative prefixed output. Preserve tool/test failure propagation and archive diagnostics on failures. Keep the library-axis step exercised after deterministic/persona metrics validate.
findings.verification: Source: https://github.com/sebahrens/mini-agent/actions/runs/34199175478 at 6021ba1. Log shows first record 'test tests::harness_eval_tests::persona_regression_eval ... PERSONA_EVAL {agent_type:rust-maintainer,...}', then eight standalone PERSONA_EVAL records and exit 1. Reproduce exact workflow command/extractor locally, assert all nine persona IDs are parsed, then dispatch the nightly workflow and verify three non-empty artifacts including both none/library arms.

findings.title: A bounded read can allocate an entire arbitrarily long source line
evidence: Explicit offset/limit allows a file larger than max_text_file_size to pass the initial gate. read_until(newline, &mut raw_line) then grows a Vec until newline/EOF without a byte bound; only afterwards is the excerpt size checked. A 1-line request against a multi-GB minified file can OOM the parent before returning its otherwise helpful size-limit error. Skipped lines before the requested offset allocate the same way.
findings.required_change: Read lines incrementally with a bounded buffer. For selected lines, fail as soon as the byte budget is exceeded; skip/hash earlier or unselected long lines in chunks without retaining them. Preserve UTF-8 validation and hashedit whole-file CRC semantics with bounded memory. Define and test behavior for files growing during a read.
findings.verification: Code-confirmed on 6021ba1: explicit limit bypasses metadata rejection; tokio AsyncBufReadExt::read_until receives an unbounded Vec at read.rs:193; the first cap check is read.rs:231. Use a chunked/counting reader or allocation instrumentation with a single line far larger than the cap, requesting limit=1 and then offset past the line. Assert bounded peak retained memory and no allocation proportional to source line size; cover CRLF and incremental UTF-8/CRC. Run cargo test read.

findings.title: Default provider streams have no connection or inactivity deadline
evidence: Provider clients set a total timeout only when an optional custom-provider timeout_secs is present. The locked reqwest 0.13.4 defaults connect_timeout, read_timeout and timeout to None. Main/headless/advisor loops await the provider stream without an independent inactivity deadline. A peer that accepts the request and stalls before headers or between SSE events can keep a turn alive indefinitely; retry logic is never entered because no error arrives.
findings.required_change: Introduce explicit configurable provider connect and stream-inactivity bounds with documented defaults, applied to built-in and custom providers. Keep long healthy streams alive by resetting the inactivity deadline on valid progress. Route deadline failures through bounded retry/cancellation and preserve already executed tool history and usage; make headless termination actionable.
findings.verification: Code-confirmed against the locked dependency: reqwest-0.13.4/src/async_impl/client.rs:299,313-314 defaults all three to None; build_http_client only sets timeout at provider.rs:1597 under custom Some(secs); production stream consumers have no idle select. Add hermetic servers that accept then stall before headers and after one SSE event, a slow healthy stream, custom override tests, and main/headless/advisor deadline recovery tests. Assert bounded retries and no duplicated effects.

findings.title: Concurrent hook decisions overwrite another call's required approval
evidence: PermissionChecker keeps only one pending_forced_ask and one pending_one_shot_allow for the entire checker. Scoped tokens prevent another invocation consuming a decision, but a second hook overwrites the first decision before its tool checks permissions. Two concurrent read calls using the production concurrency wrapper and a barrier before check_perm, each with a PreToolUse ask verdict, produced one denied call and one successful call in noninteractive Standard mode. Both must deny without an approval channel.
findings.required_change: Store hook decisions per invocation token or within the invocation task-local scope, without overwriting other in-flight calls. Ensure cancellation, early return and completion remove only that invocation's state. Preserve deny-rule precedence and single-use semantics; keep read-tool concurrency.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-hooks.patch and run cargo test --features hooks,skills release_review_probe_parallel_read_hooks_keep_both_ask_decisions -- --nocapture. Currently one call succeeds. Require both calls to deny without ask_tx and both to request independent approval with an interactive channel. Add mixed ask/allow/defer, same/different tool names, opposite scheduling orders and cancellation tests; assert no cross-call decision loss or reuse.

findings.title: Hook approval decisions are ignored when tools use different permission keys or no inner check
evidence: HookedTool records ask/allow against the public ToolDyn name and assumes an inner permission check will consume it. Git checks git/status etc. while its public name is git; MCP checks mcp_tool while its public name is the discovered tool name. SkillsSearchTool and AdvisorTool have no inner check, and todo_write returns Allowed before reading the pending decision. A wrapped fixture using git -> git/status succeeded after an ask verdict without ask_tx; a wrapped tool with no inner permission check also succeeded. The two probes exercise the real decorator/checker contract with fixture tools, not real Git/advisor operations.
findings.required_change: Enforce hook approval decisions for every wrapped invocation, using an explicit contract between decorator and permission checks that supports operation-specific keys and tools without inner checks. An ask must never silently fall through: prompt once before execution or fail closed if approval is unavailable. Honor allow for the intended invocation while preserving explicit deny rules, path scopes and operation-specific policy; do not solve this by indiscriminate tool-name widening.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-hooks.patch and run cargo test --features hooks,skills release_review_probe_hook_ask_covers -- --nocapture. Both probes currently return success where denial is required. Add production integration coverage for Git status and commit, namespaced MCP tools, todo_write and a tool without an inner check. Cover interactive/headless/missing checker paths, allow/ask/deny, rewritten input and explicit deny precedence. Assert a denied ask executes no side effects.

findings.title: Post-tool hooks receive original arguments after a pre-hook input rewrite
evidence: PreToolUse updated_input is serialized and passed to the inner tool, but both PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure receive the original parsed tool_input. A real hook subprocess rewriting path from original-target to actual-target made the tool return actual-target while the post-hook JSON still reported original-target. Post hooks that audit or validate the affected file/command therefore inspect a different operation from the one executed.
findings.required_change: Retain the effective serialized/parsed arguments actually passed to the inner tool and send those to both success and failure post hooks. If original input is needed for provenance, expose it separately with documented semantics. Keep chained pre-hook rewrites and non-rewritten calls consistent.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-hooks.patch and run cargo test --features hooks,skills release_review_probe_post_hook_observes_executed_rewritten_input -- --nocapture. Currently the post envelope contains original-target. Require actual-target and add failure-path and multiple-rewrite tests that compare the captured inner-tool arguments with post-hook input; verify unchanged input when no rewrite occurs.

findings.title: A transient skill-store startup failure is cached as healthy and never recovers
evidence: SkillRuntime::open_with_learned_js converts coordinator/catalog startup errors into None components but returns Ok. SkillSessionServices also converts observation/proposal failures into None and returns Ok. WorkspaceServiceCache only retries an overall Err, so it permanently caches this partial bundle as healthy. In a real SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE probe with one installed skill, startup under contention completed with zero learned skills; after ROLLBACK and expiry of retry backoff, the next resolve and prompt still had zero skills and cache.failure() returned None. The per-open FTS probe performs schema writes and maps database-busy errors to MissingFts5, making ordinary writer contention sufficient to trigger this path.
findings.required_change: Represent partial startup health explicitly and retry transiently unavailable learned-index, catalog, observation and proposal components with bounded backoff. Preserve working components and independent turn state, but do not mark a degraded bundle permanently healthy. Surface component disablement to the operator, preserve the underlying database error class and ensure recovery installs each worker only once. Keep permanently unavailable configurations bounded and do not inject operational diagnostics into model prompts.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-skill-startup.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_busy_startup_recovers_learned_skills_after_unlock -- --nocapture. Currently it fails with index length 0 instead of 1 and diagnostic=None. Require retrieval to recover on a later turn after a real SQLite writer releases its lock, without recreating the whole session. Cover each partial component independently, permanent failure, concurrent resolvers and cancellation; assert bounded attempts and no duplicate workers.

findings.title: Skill observation and proposal startup block the async executor on SQLite and model initialization
evidence: open_with_paths offloads only SkillRuntime construction. It then synchronously starts telemetry and proposal services inside the async future, opening three SQLite connections and constructing embedders. Store opens run an FTS schema-write probe with a five-second busy timeout; the local backend also synchronously initializes/downloads an ONNX model. A real SQLite writer held for 400 ms delayed a 20 ms current-thread Tokio timer by 416 ms when the actual observation-startup helper ran in the same call shape as production. Main runtime startup being offloaded does not protect this tail.
findings.required_change: Move all blocking observation/proposal initialization to a tracked blocking worker with cancellation-safe ownership and bounded waiting. Keep async timers, UI and cancellation responsive while SQLite is busy or model construction is slow. Preserve session-lifetime workers and clean up any late initialization result after cancellation; do not merely shorten the SQLite timeout or reduce test parallelism.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-skill-startup.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_observation_startup_keeps_executor_responsive -- --nocapture. Currently the timer runs after 416 ms instead of near its 20 ms deadline. The probe targets the synchronous helper called directly by open_with_paths; add an end-to-end current-thread open_with_paths test with a deterministic handoff into the observation/proposal phase, real SQLite contention and a slow model initializer. Assert timely timer/cancellation progress and eventual cleanup of initialized workers.

findings.title: Proposal-enabled learned-skill sessions load the local embedding model three times
evidence: With skills-embed and backend=local, SkillRuntime construction, observation startup and admission startup each call Embedder::from_config, and every call invokes FastembedBackend::new -> TextEmbedding::try_new. Observation initializes a complete model before shared_coordinator discovers that the runtime already registered that coordinator, so this second model is immediately discarded. Runtime and admission retain separate model instances, and new sessions construct another set even when the shared coordinator exists. The three-initialization/two-retained-model result is code-confirmed; no ONNX memory or timing measurement is claimed.
findings.required_change: Share an initialized embedding backend across runtime retrieval, coordinator/telemetry and admission for one compatible embedding configuration. Avoid constructing a backend merely to look up an existing coordinator. Preserve model metadata/cache invalidation and serialize inference as required by the backend; do not share incompatible provider/configuration identities. Give shared models a bounded lifetime.
findings.verification: Add a counting backend factory or equivalent construction seam and open a production-shaped service bundle with proposals enabled: assert exactly one expensive backend initialization and reuse by retrieval and admission. With skills-embed and a cached local model, measure startup and resident memory before/after, verify identical embeddings/retrieval, concurrent inference and release on session teardown. Cover changes in model/revision/dimensions/provider configuration so sharing cannot reuse the wrong backend.

findings.title: macOS worker cold startup and cancellation recovery exceed the recorded latency targets
evidence: The actual v1.8.0 debug resource artifact from baseline CI 34190987872 contains two matched-runner samples on macOS 26 / virtual Apple M1, each with 10 warmups and 100 measured iterations. Cold Ready p95 was 2678.268 ms then 1879.391 ms against the 300 ms target; cancel-and-recover p95 was 2172.205 ms then 1900.945 ms against 1000 ms. Warm pure calls remained 0.839/1.232 ms. The cost is concentrated in obtaining a fresh contained worker, not normal warm execution. The launcher performs publication sweep, immutable image preparation, guardian launch and authenticated Ready; which phase dominates still requires profiling. Timing targets are explicitly informational, so this is a measured performance finding rather than a failed security gate or a proven regression against another build.
findings.required_change: Profile source-free elapsed times for publication sweep, image snapshot/sealing, guardian launch and Ready authentication on the same supported macOS runner. Optimize the dominant fresh-worker costs to meet the stated cold/recovery budgets while preserving one-time executable identity, all containment checks, parent-death cleanup, zero idle runtimes and one live worker. Record matched-host before/after measurements; if the target cannot be met without weakening containment, obtain an explicit documented release performance decision instead of silently treating green CI as meeting the target.
findings.verification: Use the installed debug production binary and js_worker_resource_benchmark on supported macOS 26, retaining 10 warmups/100 samples and matched-runner repeats. Require cold Ready p95 <=300 ms and cancel-and-recover p95 <=1000 ms, or a specifically reviewed target exception backed by measurements. Re-run macOS production-binary denial/guardian/one-time-image matrices and ensure warm-call latency, memory and process/runtime counts do not regress. Existing evidence is preserved in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-platform-evidence.json with source CI/artifact IDs.

findings.title: macOS 26 CI evidence incorrectly reports that no production worker is available
evidence: The macOS evidence writer hard-codes assurance=deprecated-best-effort-fail-closed and native_resource_gate=unavailable-no-production-worker for both macos-15 and macos-26. In baseline CI 34190987872, the macos-26 artifact simultaneously says production_binary_matrix=passed, resource_measurement=recorded and no production worker; its actual resource artifact records a running seatbelt worker with deprecated-best-effort assurance. The summary therefore cannot distinguish supported-but-weaker macOS 26 containment from macOS 15 fail-closed unavailability and misreports the platform's release evidence.
findings.required_change: Generate availability, assurance and native resource evidence from the actual validated probe result, distinguishing unsupported hosts, available deprecated-best-effort containment, failed probes and not-run steps. Do not infer success solely from the matrix label or emit completed native checks after an earlier failure. Preserve source-free output and validate consistency between gate and resource artifacts.
findings.verification: Add behavior-level tests for evidence generation covering successful macOS 26, unsupported macOS 15, preflight refusal and a skipped/failed native probe. Assert that measured production-worker resources cannot coexist with unavailable-no-production-worker and that assurance matches the runtime's typed status. Run both macOS CI rows and inspect the generated JSON. Contradictory baseline artifacts are preserved in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-platform-evidence.json.

findings.title: Mid-turn skills_search removes task-outcome credit for skills invoked before the search
evidence: TaskOutcomeRecorder snapshots only the final selected skill bundle. ingest_task_outcome checks durable invocations only for IDs present in that snapshot. A real SkillRuntime probe selected and invoked a skill, re-froze the same turn with an unrelated search, and recorded a successful oracle through TaskOutcomeRecorder. The outcome persisted but had zero links to the previously invoked skill. Preserving turn_id across searches does not preserve the union of invoked skills. Utility statistics and lifecycle task evidence omit that actual invocation; an empty final bundle can also create a false no-library baseline.
findings.required_change: Attribute task outcomes to the complete set of qualified durable invocations for the parent-owned turn, independent of the latest retrieval bundle. Alternatively retain a parent-authoritative per-turn invocation set across every search. Preserve selected-but-unused exclusion, production/gym isolation, bounded cardinality, idempotency and stale/purged-revision handling.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_search_keeps_outcomes_linked_to_earlier_invocations -- --nocapture. It currently persists zero links instead of one. Cover A invoked then search B, A and B both invoked, an empty final bundle, multiple completion-verification attempts and selected-but-unused candidates. Assert task evidence and displayed utility count all actual invoked revisions once per turn.

findings.title: Lost invocation telemetry is counted as a successful no-skill baseline
evidence: When invocation events are rejected or dropped, ingest_task_outcome silently removes the unmatched skill IDs and still persists the successful task outcome. load_skill_stats interprets absence of outcome links as a no-skill baseline and does not exclude observability-lost turns. A dispatcher probe recorded one healthy linked task plus a turn with an explicit ObservabilityLost event, then successful outcomes for both. The production stats loader counted the lost-evidence turn as one baseline task instead of excluding it. A session counter/log saying positive evidence was excluded does not enforce that exclusion in durable outcomes.
findings.required_change: Persist a parent-authoritative per-turn evidence-completeness/attribution state and distinguish verified no-invocation turns from unknown/lost evidence. Exclude incomplete turns from positive utility and baseline comparisons even when no invocation row survived. Preserve real selected-but-unused/no-library baselines and make queue saturation or rejected worker telemetry update completeness without relying on the same saturated queue.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_observability_loss_is_not_a_no_skill_baseline -- --nocapture. It currently reports baseline_tasks=1 instead of0. Add rejected-worker-batch, saturated/disconnected queue, delayed persistence and clean selected-but-unused cases; verify restart persistence and production/gym separation. Assert incomplete evidence changes neither positive skill outcomes nor no-library baseline pass rates.

findings.title: Telemetry retry on a busy SQLite writer can prevent process shutdown indefinitely
evidence: ingest_retrying_busy retries forever with capped sleep but no shutdown signal or deadline. Dropping TelemetryDispatcher closes its queue and joins the worker directly or through Tokio spawn_blocking. Closing the sender cannot interrupt the in-flight busy loop; Tokio runtime destruction waits for the blocking join. A real SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE probe entered the retry loop, dropped the dispatcher, and measured runtime teardown. It waited 878.678 ms until a separate thread released the writer after700 ms; it has no terminating condition if that writer remains locked.
findings.required_change: Make telemetry shutdown cancel-aware with a bounded flush/drain policy that can interrupt busy retries and blocking waits. Preserve accepted evidence via a durable retry/outbox path or explicitly record unrecoverable observability loss; do not leave an unbounded join on the runtime blocking pool. Keep healthy-session retries reliable and avoid leaking owned workers after teardown.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_telemetry_shutdown_does_not_wait_for_external_writer -- --nocapture. The700 ms unlock is a probe watchdog, not a prescribed production deadline. Add an isolated-process test retaining the SQLite lock beyond the configured shutdown budget; require bounded exit and documented evidence recovery/loss behavior. Also verify ordinary transient contention still persists accepted batches and repeated session teardown leaves no threads.

findings.title: A failed headless turn discards completed tool history and usage after effects already ran
evidence: The headless runner accumulates tool interactions and usage, but returns a plain anyhow error when a non-retryable stream error, exhausted retry/turn/token budget or failed completion verification occurs. dispatch_print immediately propagates response_result? before persist_headless_turn, charge_usage_delta and save_session. Therefore a write/edit/command can complete, a later provider failure can terminate the turn, and the saved session contains neither the prompt nor completed tool records or incurred usage. A resumed session has no durable record of the effects and may repeat them. This finding is code-confirmed; no live provider or terminal signal test was run.
findings.required_change: Carry partial headless turn state on terminal failure, including completed tool calls/results, observed usage and interrupted pending-call markers. Persist that state and an explicit failure outcome before returning a nonzero exit code, using the same order/replay identities as successful turns. Preserve --no-session behavior and ensure partial persistence failures are reported without presenting the task as successful.
findings.verification: Add a hermetic fake-model headless-dispatch test that performs a real temporary-file edit, then emits a non-retryable error or exhausts retries. Assert nonzero/failure status while the reloaded session retains the prompt, exact completed tool record and observed usage; --continue must see the completed effect. Cover token/turn budget failure, verification failure, an unresolved tool call, JSON output and --no-session. Never convert the failure into an Ok truncated response.

findings.title: Immediate skill quarantine is lost when index publication is pending
evidence: Automatic quarantine is evaluated only for terminal events in the arriving telemetry batch. It sets generation_current from desired_generation == applied_generation; the policy holds on false and the caller only logs the error, without scheduling a retry. In a real dispatcher/coordinator probe, an active skill had a pending index generation when its Invoked and CapabilityDenied events arrived. After telemetry drained and the index rebuilt, the skill was still active and present in the published index. A single safety event can therefore be permanently ignored during ordinary publication lag, contrary to the immediate-quarantine contract.
findings.required_change: Persist and retry direct safety-triggered quarantine across publication lag and optimistic conflicts. Re-read current revision/generation state under the coordinator's mutation gate, apply the safety transition atomically, and publish a removal-only snapshot when a full rebuild is unavailable. Do not bypass stale-state checks, wait for another invocation to fail, or leave a known-unsafe revision available while a durable quarantine decision is pending.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_pending_index_generation -- --nocapture. It currently reports status=active and visible_after_rebuild=true instead of quarantine. Require a capability-denied skill to become ineligible despite desired/applied generation lag. Cover canary timeout/OOM, concurrent generation changes, rebuild failure, process restart and duplicate terminal delivery; assert a single durable transition/evidence record and no re-enable after recovery.

findings.title: ACP forgets completed tool effects when a turn fails or is cancelled
evidence: ACP forwards ToolCall and ToolResult notifications to the editor but only commits SessionHistory after AgentEvent::Done. Error, cancellation and channel-end branches return without retaining any partial interactions. An in-memory ACP protocol probe wrote a real temporary file, emitted its completed tool call/result and then a terminal error. The client correctly received Refusal, but its next prompt received history=[], despite the file still containing the completed write. The explicit cancellation branch has the same history omission; only the error path was dynamically reproduced. This is separate from headless .24 because ACP owns a different relay and session-history commit boundary.
findings.required_change: Retain a protocol-valid partial turn when ACP work fails or is cancelled after progress. Carry canonical completed tool messages, provider call IDs and reasoning from the runner, finalize unresolved calls as interrupted, and commit the prompt plus that progress before releasing the session. Preserve the Refusal/Cancelled response and preserve rollback for a cancellation before any work occurs; do not turn a failed operation into EndTurn success.
findings.verification: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-acp.patch and run cargo test --features acp,skills release_review_probe_acp -- --nocapture. Currently the next prompt receives an empty history after a completed write and refusal. Add in-memory protocol tests for cancellation after a completed tool result, channel closure, partial text/reasoning and cancellation before start; assert retained call/result pairing, cross-session isolation and unchanged generation-safe cancellation behavior.

findings.title: Skill statistics repeatedly scan task baselines and approach cubic work as history grows
evidence: For every retained revision, load_skill_stats separately counts baseline tasks and baseline passes by scanning all task outcomes and running another correlated observed-skill/source match for each baseline. A hermetic probe extracts the exact production SQL and uses a reduced SQLite schema with the relevant production indexes. With one observed task and one no-library baseline per revision under a shared oracle, 20/40/80 revisions executed approximately 177,700 / 1,215,400 / 8,942,800 VM steps: doubling data multiplied work 6.84x then 7.36x. EXPLAIN shows a baseline scan inside a correlated subquery and a further source-index search inside it. This measurement used local SQLite 3.53.2 rather than the Rust-bundled build; measured times were 3/21/174 ms and are illustrative only. An initial larger run was explicitly interrupted and is not used as completed evidence.
findings.required_change: Compute qualified outcome groups, per-skill observed source scopes and comparable baseline counts in set-based grouped queries or bounded pre-aggregations, then join the results once per revision. Avoid rescanning every baseline and every observed task for every skill. Preserve exact source-kind/source-id and production matching, distinct-turn semantics, absent-baseline n/a behavior, and exclusion of incomplete evidence required by .22.
findings.verification: Run python3 docs/reviews/2026-09-08-stats-scaling.py from the repository root; its recorded query plan and VM-step counts are in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-stats-scaling.json. Add a regression on the actual Rust-bundled SQLite/schema through load_skill_stats at increasing revision/outcome counts, verify exact utility results, and demonstrate that doubling both sets no longer multiplies query work approximately 8x. Include repeated oracle IDs, many source scopes, production/gym traffic, multiple attempts and missing baselines; report bounded latency at the documented retained-corpus scale.

residual_risks: Review and issue filing are complete for the recorded scope; the 27 implementation findings remain open. This is not release approval or a claim that the code is bug-free.

Admission authorization/optimistic transactions, lifecycle replacement, retention watermark/purge, provider retry/cancellation settlement and installer/archive/MSI source contracts received a final source/test-coverage pass. No additional defect was confirmed beyond the filed findings. Full cross-platform installer execution and exhaustive concurrency exploration were not performed locally. Canonical worker/broker/containment boundaries received source, hostile-test and dedicated CI artifact review; this is not a proof against every possible native exploit.

Linux/Windows runtime behavior has not been exercised locally, but baseline CI containment and resource artifacts were downloaded and inspected, including Windows standard-user evidence. These establish behavior on the recorded runners only. The macOS gate-summary inconsistency is tracked in .20.
Performance test failure in the restricted initial run was not reproduced in the unrestricted full suite; no separate performance-regression finding was inferred from that timing sample.
testing_gaps: Twenty targeted Rust regressions covering nineteen findings are preserved as opt-in patches, outside the ordinary passing suite. They assert desired behavior and currently fail.
Read long-line allocation and provider-inactivity findings are code-confirmed; implementation beads require instrumented/hermetic regressions.
Nightly workflow policy tests assert command strings, not correctness of record extraction.
Repeated local embedding-model construction is code-confirmed; construction-count and ONNX memory measurements are acceptance work for .18.
Headless failure persistence (.24) is code-confirmed; its bead requires a hermetic fake-model test across runner failure and saved-session reload.
ACP error-after-effect history loss (.26) was reproduced in memory; cancellation shares the source omission and still needs the explicit regression required by its bead.

Statistics scaling (.27) was measured using exact production SQL and relevant indexes on a reduced system-SQLite fixture; actual Rust-bundled SQLite/schema performance is required acceptance work. The saved script bounds each sample to 50 million VM steps.
objective: Thorough release code review covering bugs, issues and performance bottlenecks, with atomic beads specifying what to change, where and how to verify.
